references.text: Also here in Luke, the evangelist describes how large crowds gathered around Jesus: "However, people had gathered by thousands" ([ref:Luk 12:1|Luke 12:1]). Large crowds followed Jesus throughout his ministry.

Jesus turned to the crowd to teach about what it truly means to follow him, a theme that continues in [ref:Luk 14:26-27|Luke 14:26-27]. Here Jesus says: "If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me" ([ref:Luk 9:23-27|Luke 9:23-27]).
Matthew similarly describes how large crowds followed Jesus: "Great crowds followed him" ([ref:Matt 19:2|Matthew 19:2]). This shows the recurring pattern of large numbers seeking out Jesus.

Jesus makes similar radical demands for discipleship in the Gospel of Matthew, which closely aligns with what Jesus says to the crowd after this verse: "Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me" ([ref:Matt 10:37-38|Matthew 10:37-38]).
Mark also tells of large crowds gathering around Jesus, whom he taught: "People gathered again around him, and as was his custom, he taught them once more" ([ref:Mark 10:1|Mark 10:1]).

What follows after Jesus turned to the crowd is his radical teaching on the conditions for being his disciple—hating one's family, carrying one's cross, and giving up everything ([ref:Luk 14:26-33|Luke 14:26-33]). Verse 25 serves as an introduction to this teaching.

In the Gospel of John, it is also described how a large crowd followed Jesus: "A great crowd followed him" ([ref:Joh 6:2|John 6:2]). The crowds followed him, but many left when his words became too demanding (see [ref:Joh 6:66|John 6:66]).
